help.catalog: The catalog-wide default for detecting write conflicts. It applies to every collection and entity in this catalog unless an entity declares its own policy. If unset, the engine-wide default configured on this server is used.
help.entity: How write conflicts are detected for this entity type. If set here it overrides the catalog and engine defaults entirely (scope and refinements). It applies to every attribute, reference and associated data of this entity unless one of them declares its own override.

effectiveScope.entity: The conflict scope actually applied to writes of this {item}, after resolving the entity policy and this override.
effectiveScope.catalog: The conflict scope actually applied to writes of this {item}, after resolving the catalog policy and this override.

help.granularIntro: Granular refinements narrow checking to a single part of an entity, so two people editing different parts of the same entity no longer clash — fewer rejections, higher throughput. The trade-off: two edits to different parts can now both succeed, so use them only where those parts don't depend on each other.
help.colorLegend: Colour shows how widely evitaDB looks for a conflicting change: wider (red) rejects more of your concurrent saves — safer but slower; narrower lets more through — faster but relaxes a safety check.

none.label: No detection
none.hint: Conflict detection is turned off. Concurrent saves never clash, so nothing is ever rejected — but when two of them change the same data, whichever saves last silently overwrites the other and the first change is lost with no warning. The fastest option and the least safe; use only when losing a concurrent update is acceptable.

catalog.label: Catalog-wide
catalog.short: Any change anywhere in the catalog clashes
catalog.hint: The widest net. Two saves clash if they change anything in the catalog — even unrelated entities in different collections. Strongest consistency, but effectively only one write per catalog version survives, so most concurrent saves are rejected and must retry. Shown red because that high rejection rate means the lowest write throughput. Use only for operations that need a frozen snapshot of the whole catalog (bulk import, global re-pricing).

collection.label: Collection-wide
collection.short: Any change to this entity type clashes
collection.hint: Two saves clash if they change any entity of the same type — two Product edits clash even on different products, while a Product edit and a Category edit run side by side. Use it to guard a rule spanning the whole collection that has no single owning entity (e.g. only one product may be the storefront hero). It serializes the whole collection, so throughput drops — hence the warning colour.

entity.label: Per entity
entity.short: Only changes to the same entity clash
entity.hint: The recommended default and the best balance of safety and speed. Two saves clash only when they change the same entity (same type and primary key); edits to two different products never clash. It is also the only scope you can narrow further with the granular refinements.

entityAttribute.label: Per attribute
entityAttribute.short: Same-attribute edits clash; different-attribute edits don't
entityAttribute.hint: Two saves to the same entity clash only if they change the same attribute — changing name and price at once no longer clashes, but two edits to name still do.

levelNote.entity: On an entity: applies to every attribute of this entity unless a specific attribute overrides it.
levelNote.catalog: On the catalog: applies to every attribute of every entity in the catalog unless an entity or attribute overrides it.

associatedData.label: Per associated data
associatedData.short: Only edits to the same associated-data item clash
associatedData.hint: Two saves clash only if they change the same associated-data item; edits to different associated data of the same entity run side by side. Applies to all associated data below this level unless an item overrides it.

price.label: Per price
price.short: Only edits to the same price clash
price.hint: Two saves clash only if they change the same price; edits to different prices of the same entity run side by side. Applies to all prices below this level. (No per-price override exists — set it here.)

hierarchy.label: Per hierarchy move
hierarchy.short: Only two moves of the same entity clash
hierarchy.hint: Two saves clash only if they both change this entity's position in the tree; other edits run alongside a move. (No per-item override — set it here.)

reference.label: Per reference
reference.short: Only edits to the same reference clash
reference.hint: Two saves clash only if they change the same reference; edits to different references of the same entity run side by side. Applies to all references below this level unless a reference overrides it.

referenceAttribute.label: Per reference attribute
referenceAttribute.short: Only edits to the same attribute of the same reference clash
referenceAttribute.hint: Even finer than Per reference: two saves clash only if they change the same attribute on the same reference. Applies to all reference attributes below this level unless one overrides it.

granular.label: Granular
granular.hint: This {item} gets its own conflict check: a save clashes with another only when both change this {item}; every other change to the entity ignores it. Overrides what the entity policy would do for this {item}. Only takes effect while the entity is checked Per entity — if the entity is No detection / Catalog-wide / Collection-wide, this override does nothing.

entity.label: Whole entity
entity.short: Always clash with any change to the entity
entity.hint: This {item} is pinned to whole-entity checking: any concurrent change to the same entity clashes with it, even when the rest of the entity uses finer per-part checks. Use it for a consistency-critical {item} you never want changed behind your back.

inertWarning.entity: No effect — this entity is checked {scope}, which is wider than Per entity, so this override is ignored. Overrides only apply when the entity's effective scope is Per entity.
inertWarning.catalog: No effect — this catalog is checked {scope}, which is wider than Per entity, so this override is ignored. Overrides only apply when the effective scope is Per entity.

notification.failedToResolvePolicy: Could not resolve the effective conflict resolution policy

thisItemOnly.label: This {item} only
thisItemOnly.hint: A save is rejected only if another concurrent save changes this same {item}.

wholeEntity.label: Whole entity
wholeEntity.hint: A save is rejected if any concurrent save changes this entity.

noDetection.label: No detection (last writer wins)
noDetection.hint: Conflict detection is off for this entity — concurrent changes are never rejected and the last save wins, so changes can be lost.

wholeCatalog.label: Whole catalog
wholeCatalog.hint: A save is rejected if any concurrent save changes anything in the catalog.

wholeCollection.label: Whole collection
wholeCollection.hint: A save is rejected if any concurrent save changes any entity of this type.

definedHere.label: Defined here
definedHere.hint: This policy is set directly on this {level}.

inheritedFromCatalog.label: Inherited from catalog
inheritedFromCatalog.hint: No policy is set on this entity, so it uses the catalog's policy. Set one here to override it for this entity type.

engineDefault.label: Engine default
engineDefault.hint: No policy is set on this catalog or entity, so the engine-wide default configured on this server ({scope}) applies.

followsEntityPolicy.label: Follows entity policy

backup.title: Backup catalog
backup.info: The back up process may take a while. Therefore it will be started asynchronously. You can find it’s progress and backup file to download in task listing.

includeWal.label: Include WAL
includeWal.description: Will apply all mutations from WAL during restoration resulting in the latest version of catalog

full.title: Full backup
full.description: A full backup will contain a binary copy of all catalog files at the current time. After restoring the catalog from this backup, it will also be possible to perform additional "point-in-time" backups from this restored copy for all moments for which historical data is available. This full backup is the largest backup of the catalog in size.

pointInTime.title: Point in time backup
pointInTime.description: A point in time backup contains only data valid at the point in time (version) of the catalog that is selected when the backup is created. When going back in time, it is only possible to select a point in time for which the database still has historical data. In order to protect against running out of disk capacity, historical data is deleted after some time / reaching a limit size. A catalog restored from this backup will not allow point in time recovery, or will only allow it over other write operations performed over the restored catalog.

snapshot.title: Current snapshot backup
snapshot.description: The current snapshot contains only currently valid data. It is the smallest possible functional backup, which also makes it the fastest backup option. A catalog restored from this backup will not allow point-in-time recovery, or will only allow recovery over other write operations performed on the restored catalog.

button.exportTrafficBufferHelp: Downloads a point-in-time snapshot of the rolling traffic buffer the server keeps in memory. No recording needs to be running; the snapshot covers whatever fits into the buffer window at this moment.
button.exportTrafficBufferUnavailable: Traffic recording is not active for this catalog, so there is no traffic buffer to export. Enable traffic recording in the server configuration, or start an on-demand recording in Traffic Recordings.

exportDialog.title: Export traffic buffer
exportDialog.info: The server keeps a rolling buffer of recent traffic in memory. This exports its current content into a downloadable archive as a point-in-time snapshot — no recording needs to be running and any running recording is not affected.

hint.default: The size of the chunk file in bytes. Individual files in the export archive will be approximately this size. Leave empty to use the server default. You can use k, M, G, Ki, Mi, or Gi unit prefix.
hint.rounded: The size of the chunk file will be rounded to full bytes.

validations.notByteSize: Chunk file size must be byte size.
validations.outOfRange: Chunk file size must be positive number and less than 2^63-1.

since.label: Since
since.hint: Specifies the time from which the history should be returned.

types.label: Types
types.hint: Specifies the types of records to be returned.

sessionId.label: Session ID
sessionId.hint: Specifies the session ID from which the history should be returned.

validations.notUuid: Session ID must be a UUID.

longerThan.label: Longer than
longerThan.hint: Specifies the minimum duration in milliseconds of the traffic recording to be returned. Use combination of h, min, s, or ms units.

validations.outOfRange: Threshold must be positive number and less than 2^53-1.

fetchingMoreBytesThan.label: Fetching more bytes than
fetchingMoreBytesThan.hint: Specifies the minimum number of bytes that record should have fetched from the disk. You can use k, M, G, Ki, Mi, or Gi unit prefix.

validations.outOfRange: Threshold must be positive number and less than 2^53-1.

labels.label: Labels
labels.hint: Specifies the client labels that the record must have (both name and value must match).

info.noActiveTrafficRecording: Traffic recording is not active for the {catalogName} catalog, so there is no traffic buffer to inspect or export. You need to either enable traffic recording in the server configuration or start recording on demand in traffic recordings.
info.indexCreating: Index is being created for the active traffic recording for the {catalogName} catalog. Please wait and reload history in a few moments.
info.noRecords: There are no traffic records for defined filter. The traffic buffer of the {catalogName} catalog may still hold records excluded by the filter — use the "Export traffic buffer" action in the toolbar to download a snapshot of its entire content.
